problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.

Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. You can return the two indices in any order.
hints: For each number x, the partner you need is target - x.
A dictionary from value to index lets you find that partner in O(1).

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description:
Given a string s containing only the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', decide whether it is valid.

A string is valid if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets are closed in the correct order.
hints: Push opening brackets onto a stack.
When you see a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be its matching opener.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is a stock's price on day i.

Choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the maximum profit you can make. If no profit is possible, return 0.
hints: Track the lowest price seen so far.
At each day, the best sale is today's price minus that lowest price.

examples.explanation: Buy at 1 on day 2, sell at 6 on day 5: profit 5
Prices only fall, so no profit is possible

problems.solution:
def maxProfit(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    lowest = float('inf')
    best = 0
    for p in prices:
        lowest = min(lowest, p)
        best = max(best, p - lowest)
    return best

    return best

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description:
Given two strings s and t, return True if t is an anagram of s, and False otherwise.

An anagram uses exactly the same letters the same number of times, in any order.
hints: Count how many times each letter appears in each string.
Two strings are anagrams exactly when the counts match.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers nums and an integer target, return the index of target, or -1 if it is not present.

Your solution should run in O(log n) time.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order
hints: Compare target with the middle element.
Discard the half that cannot contain target.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.
hints: At each index, decide: extend the previous subarray, or start fresh here?
This is Kadane's algorithm and runs in O(n).

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum, 6

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.description:
You are given coin denominations coins and a total amount. You have an unlimited supply of each coin.

Return the fewest coins needed to make up amount. If it cannot be made, return -1.
hints: Let dp[a] be the fewest coins that make amount a.
dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]) over every coin c <= a.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that has no repeated characters.
constraints: s may contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces
hints: Keep a window [left, right] with no repeats.
Remember the last index of each character to jump left forward in one step.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.description:
Given a 2D grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands.

An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically. Everything outside the grid is water.
hints: Scan every cell. When you find unvisited land, that's a new island.
Use BFS or DFS to mark the whole island as visited.

examples.explanation: All land cells are connected through the middle

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i].

Solve it in O(n) time without using division.
hints: answer[i] = (product of everything to the left) x (product of everything to the right).
Compute left products in one pass and right products in a second pass.
problems.solution:
def productExceptSelf(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums)
    ans = [1] * n
    left = 1
    for i in range(n):
        ans[i] = left
        left *= nums[i]
    right = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        ans[i] *= right
        right *= nums[i]
    return ans

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where each bar has width 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hints: Water above bar i = min(tallest bar to its left, tallest to its right) - height[i].
Two pointers moving inward can compute this in O(n) time and O(1) space.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.description:
Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2, return the median of the two arrays combined.

Aim for O(log(m + n)) time.
hints: Binary search for a partition of the shorter array.
A partition is correct when every element on the left side is <= every element on the right side.

problems.title: Edit Distance
problems.description:
Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations needed to turn word1 into word2.

Allowed operations: insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character.
hints: Let dp[i][j] be the answer for the first i letters of word1 and the first j letters of word2.
If the letters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise it's 1 + the min of the three neighbours.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.description: Given an array heights representing a histogram where every bar has width 1, return the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram.
hints: For each bar, find how far the rectangle of its height can stretch left and right.
A stack of increasing heights finds all those boundaries in O(n).

examples.explanation: Bars 5 and 6 form a rectangle of height 5 and width 2: area 10

problems.solution:
def largestRectangleArea(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    stack = []
    best = 0
    for i, h in enumerate(heights + [0]):
        start = i
        while stack and stack[-1][1] >= h:
            idx, height = stack.pop()
            best = max(best, height * (i - idx))
            start = idx
        stack.append((start, h))
    return best

            start = idx
        stack.append((start, h))
    return best

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.description:
Transform beginWord into endWord by changing one letter at a time. Every intermediate word must be in wordList.

Return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence (including beginWord and endWord), or 0 if no sequence exists.
constraints: All words have the same length
hints: Think of each word as a node. Words one letter apart share an edge.
BFS from beginWord finds the shortest path.

examples.explanation: hit -> hot -> dot -> dog -> cog has 5 words
